why: Intro to Git and GitHub plan (docs/ui-next/catalog/plans/intro-git.json), 'Stage and commit' (passes: the repository has one commit and it adds pancakes.md). The learner first tried to commit the untracked file by path (`git commit -m "Add pancakes" pancakes.md` -> 'error: pathspec ... did not match any file(s) known to git'), then did it the lesson's way: git add, git commit -> '[main (root-commit) a1b2c3d] Add pancakes ... create mode 100644 pancakes.md', and `git log --oneline` shows the one commit. The error is from before the commit that worked. Done.

step.title: Commit pancakes.md
step.instructions: Stage pancakes.md with git add pancakes.md, then commit it with git commit -m "Add pancakes". git log --oneline should show one commit.

files.cookbook/pancakes.md:
# Pancakes

- 1 cup flour
- 1 cup milk
- 2 eggs
- pinch of salt

Terminal: tripi@mac cookbook % git commit -m "Add pancakes" pancakes.md
error: pathspec 'pancakes.md' did not match any file(s) known to git
